t: Lisbon grew from an Iron Age settlement on the Castelo hill that traded with the Phoenicians into the Roman municipium of Olisipo and, after the 8th century, the Muslim city of al-Us̲h̲būna, which Afonso I conquered in 1147.

It became the capital of Portugal in the 13th century and, from the end of the 15th century, the port from which most Portuguese expeditions set out, trading in spices, slaves, sugar and textiles between Africa, India, the Far East and Brazil.
The earthquake of 1 November 1755 destroyed 85 percent of its buildings, and the lower town was rebuilt on a rectangular plan under the Marquis of Pombal.
dyk: Pombal's planners tested architectural models for the rebuilt Baixa by having troops march around them to simulate an earthquake.
ev: Iron Age people occupy the Castelo hill and trade with the Phoenicians
Decimus Junius Brutus Callaicus brings Olissipo into the Roman empire
Muslim forces take the city, which becomes al-Us̲h̲būna
Afonso I conquers Lisbon with the help of crusaders
Lisbon replaces Coimbra as the capital of Portugal
Vasco da Gama sails for India
An earthquake kills an estimated 30,000 to 40,000 people and destroys 85 percent of the city's structures
The Carnation Revolution, launched in Lisbon, ends the Estado Novo

f.founded: Iron Age people occupied the Castelo hill from the 8th to 6th centuries BCE and traded with the Phoenicians; a legend names the mythical Ulysses as founder.
f.where: On the northern shore of the Tagus, near its mouth, in the western part of the Iberian Peninsula, in present-day Portugal.
f.known: The Roman port of Olisipo; Muslim al-Us̲h̲būna; the conquest of 1147; the capital of Portugal; the departure of Portuguese voyages of discovery; the spice and slave trades; the earthquake of 1755; the Pombaline Baixa
f.today: Lisbon is the capital and most populous city of Portugal.
